text: There is no direct scientific literature supporting a specific interaction between Penicillin G and Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) in the context of Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL). Penicillin G is a beta-lactam antibiotic that functions by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis via transpeptidase binding, whereas BTK is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase essential for B-cell receptor signaling and survival in MCL. Given their distinct chemical structures and biological targets, there is no established mechanistic basis for Penicillin G to act as a BTK inhibitor or therapeutic agent in MCL. Any observed clinical correlation would likely be incidental rather than a result of direct molecular interaction.
